correctness.rationale: For distinct parameters the product of chord lengths cancels the absolute Vandermonde in four times the area, giving the continuous pair-sum product in RESULT.md (1). Its factors give the unique minimum and the two same-sign maximizing corners. The continuous image of the cube is an interval, all its support values have positive-probability neighborhoods even after discarding the diagonals, and each level has volume zero (the squared radius is a polynomial nonconstant in u1 for fixed u2,u3). Independently, use s=(u1+u2,u1+u3,u2+u3), absolute determinant 2, then s_i=sgn(x_i)sqrt(exp(x_i^2)-1). The lower event is a ball of squared radius q=2 log(1+2 epsilon) in the x coordinates and has u-volume (2 pi/3)q^(3/2)+(3 pi/10)q^(5/2)+O(q^(7/2)): the Jacobian is (1/2)(1+3||x||^2/4+O(||x||^4)). Expansion gives 16 pi/3 and 8 pi/5 before dividing by 8a^3. The rescaled u sublevel sets converge in volume to the quadratic ellipsoid with matrix I+11^T, hence in total variation for the normalized conditional densities. At either maximizing corner, the inward loss is c_a sum d_i + O_a(||d||^2), with c_a=2a sqrt(1+4a^2)>0. Compact localization and this linear bound force d=O_a(epsilon); the scaled simplex can be sandwiched between sum cutoffs 1±O_a(epsilon). Two corner factors, simplex volume 1/6 and cube volume 8a^3 give the asserted upper coefficient and remainder. Reflection gives an exactly fair sign and matching reflected shapes once localized, hence the joint conditional limit. Independent replay at a=0.7 gave 165 exact determinant-distance checks; at epsilon=1e-5 the lower volume correction and upper probability coefficient were 5.026500974 and 0.008693108 against 5.026548246 and 0.008693066.
residual_risks: The replay numerically corroborates only bounded cases; the analytic sublevel arguments establish the asymptotics. Constants depend on fixed a>0. Uniform arclength and the minimum enclosing disk are not covered.

value.rationale: For a natural uniform-coordinate sampling model on a curved graph, the radius does not diverge at degenerate limiting triangles. The result distinguishes two quantitatively different coalescence mechanisms, gives a non-leading volume correction and the two conditional shapes. These are useful benchmarks for endpoint probability and geometry rather than just recalculating the classical radius identity.
residual_risks: Narrow fixed-arc model, not a full CDF, an arclength-sampling result, or a general theorem on planar curves.
